## Data Science Reflection

∗ **What do you think being a data scientist is about?** ∗ **What differences/similarities do you see between data scientists and statisticians?** ∗ **How do you view yourself in relation to these two areas?**

A data scientist solves real-world problems centered around data. They answer questions that usually support business decisions. They typically require domain knowledge in that field as well as some level of statistical understanding; without a proper statistical background they tend to interpret their computational work incorrectly. Statisticians tend to focus more on theoretical math or mathematical foundations, uncertainty, and formal modeling. I view myself as someone who's learning how to balance the best of both worlds.

## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
# Kernel Density Estimate
y <- density(iris$Petal.Width)

# Determine the class, type, and structure of y
class(y)
typeof(y)
str(y)
```

## Visualization of Object 'y'

```{r}
#| echo: false
# Plot Function on Y
plot(y, main="Density Estimate of Iris Petal Width", xlab = "Petal Width")
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
